231: Even to speak words of wisdom: And all the more so, if his speaking is about buying and selling must his intention be for the sake of a commandment. That is, that he have with what to support himself so that he not come to theft. And even if he is very wealthy, such that he has enough to support himself and the members of his household all the days of his life, it is also sometimes conceivable that his efforts to increase his business dealings are the matter of a commandment. For example, if his intention is to give much charity and communal aid as a result of this. Or if his intention is to bring businesses under his control to find work for poor Jews, so that they be hired to give them a livelihood. For all of this is in the category of charity and is greater than it, as Rambam writes and is brought down in Yoreh Deah 251, see there. For one who strengthens the hand of a Jew who has become impoverished and gives him work in order that he earn a wage and not need to beg from people, thereby fulfills the positive commandment of, and his hand falters beside you, then shall you support him (Leviticus 25:35).
